works.headline: Operational systems, built around how the work actually runs.
works.description: Four case studies from client and freelance work: the workflow, the decisions, and the parts that had to hold.

items.title: ORDER FULFILLMENT
items.description: Orders that mix stocked items with special purchases, and the state transitions that keep stock, approvals, and delivery in sync.

items.title: FINANCIAL LEDGERS
items.description: Deposits, withdrawals, and sales that must reconcile to one record, including historical imports and backdated entries.

items.title: MULTI-ROLE HANDOFFS
items.description: Work that crosses sales, warehouse, finance, and admin, where every handoff needs an owner and an audit trail.

items.title: FIELD AND MOBILE WORK
items.description: Mobile tools for agents and vendors who work away from a desk, with deadlines and state that survive bad connectivity.

items.title: REPORTING AND CONTROL
items.description: Reports, approvals, and health checks that show whether the numbers still agree after the work is done.

projects.title: ORDER OPERATIONS SYSTEM
projects.headline: One order, multiple fulfillment paths.
projects.problemHeadline: Orders were simple on paper. Fulfillment was fragmented.
projects.problemLead: A single order rarely follows one path. Some items are in stock, others must be purchased, and fragmented communication loses track of both.
projects.description: An order operations platform that connects sales, purchasing, warehouse, inventory, and finance around one order lifecycle.
projects.summary: One order can mix items already in stock with items that still need purchasing. The system gives each item its own path, then requires warehouse and finance approval before dispatch.
problemPoints: A single customer order contains items available in warehouse inventory alongside items requiring third-party procurement.
Without transactional state synchrony, stock gets double-promised and shipments leave before credit and physical verification.
Fragmented departmental handoffs obscure accountability between purchasing lead times and customer delivery promises.

overview.problem: In multi-department operations, one order can contain items already in stock and items that still need purchasing. When sales, purchasing, warehouse, inventory, and finance work from separate records, stock gets double-promised, goods arrive without assignment, and deliveries leave before credit is checked. The system had to model both paths explicitly and keep inventory and approval state in sync.
overview.approach: Each order is an active state machine with per-item branching. Stocked items are reserved immediately; unavailable items open a purchase request and vendor purchase order. Warehouse and finance approvals are separate state transitions, so a delivery order cannot be issued until both are recorded. The model follows the physical workflow, not an abstract data diagram.
overview.architecture: PostgreSQL and Prisma hold the operational tables, with transactions wrapping every state change so concurrent reservations cannot race. Nine roles limit each action to the right department. Zod validates input on client and server, and MinIO stores goods receipts and delivery notes.
overview.workflow: A confirmed sales order checks every line item. In-stock goods go to reservation; backordered items become a purchase request and then a purchase order. A goods receipt updates inventory at the dock. Before dispatch, the warehouse confirms packing and finance confirms payment or credit. Only then does the system issue the delivery order.

flowPaths.title: Item in stock
flowPaths.description: Immediate inventory reservation bypassing procurement chains entirely.

steps.name: Sales Order Confirmed
steps.action: Line item confirmed & live stock reservation triggered

steps.name: Stock reserved
steps.action: Row-level hold in database transaction locks allocated quantity

steps.name: Two approvals
steps.action: Physical readiness check + financial credit terms verified

steps.name: Delivery Order Released
steps.action: Official dispatch notice created and warehouse balance debited

flowPaths.title: Item needs purchase
flowPaths.description: Automated replenishment chain connecting Purchase Requests to warehouse floor receipts.

steps.name: Purchase Request
steps.action: Backordered items branch into an internal procurement requisition

steps.name: Vendor Purchase Order
steps.action: Formal PO dispatched to supplier with agreed lead times

steps.name: Goods Receipt
steps.action: Physical receiving at loading dock immediately increments stock

steps.name: Delivery Convergence
steps.action: Procured items converge with existing stock for packing

flowPaths.title: Two-step approval
flowPaths.description: Eliminates premature dispatches through mandatory sequential operational and financial approval.

steps.name: Delivery Request
steps.action: Initiated once all items in the sales order are ready on the floor

steps.name: Gate 1: Warehouse Sign-off
steps.action: Physical inspection verifies package integrity and packing slip

steps.name: Gate 2: Finance Clearance
steps.action: Finance officer approves customer payment receipt or credit standing

steps.name: Authorized Dispatch
steps.action: Formal delivery order unlocked; shipment authorized for departure

workflowStages.name: SALES ORDER
workflowStages.detail: Customer order confirmed. Line items are evaluated individually rather than as a monolithic order.

workflowStages.name: FULFILLMENT ROUTING
workflowStages.detail: In-stock items trigger immediate stock reservation. Out-of-stock items branch into a Purchase Request and vendor Purchase Order.

workflowStages.name: RECEIVING & INVENTORY
workflowStages.detail: Purchased items enter the warehouse via Goods Receipt, immediately incrementing available inventory without administrative delay.

workflowStages.name: DUAL-GATE APPROVAL
workflowStages.detail: Delivery Request requires sequential sign-off: Warehouse confirms physical stock readiness, then Finance clears credit and payment terms.

workflowStages.name: DISPATCH & COMPLETION
workflowStages.detail: Formal Delivery Order generated, physical goods released, inventory balances adjusted, and order marked complete.

decisions.title: PER-ITEM FULFILLMENT SPLIT
decisions.decision: Evaluates each line item within a Sales Order independently, routing in-stock items to reservation and backordered items to procurement.
decisions.rationale: Customer orders frequently contain both immediately available goods and items requiring vendor procurement. Forcing an entire order into a single fulfillment track creates unnecessary customer delays.

decisions.title: DIRECT GOODS RECEIPT TO INVENTORY
decisions.decision: Increments inventory availability directly upon physical warehouse Goods Receipt confirmation.
decisions.rationale: Separates physical receiving from vendor invoicing schedules, ensuring warehouse inventory reflects actual floor availability without administrative delay.

decisions.title: DUAL-ROLE DISPATCH APPROVAL
decisions.decision: Requires sequential authorizations from Warehouse (physical inspection) and Finance (credit and payment standing) before generating a Delivery Order.
decisions.rationale: Prevents goods from leaving the loading dock before both physical readiness is verified and customer credit terms are validated.

decisions.title: TRANSACTIONAL ROLE BOUNDARIES
decisions.decision: Enforces all cross-department handoffs through database transactions and role-based permissions spanning nine operational roles.
decisions.rationale: Prevents race conditions during simultaneous stock reservations and maintains an auditable chain of custody across departmental transitions.

highlights: Per-item state machine supporting independent reservation and procurement paths per order line.
Direct Goods Receipt to inventory ingestion keeping stock availability synchronized with physical receiving.
Role-gated dual approval requiring both Warehouse and Finance authorization prior to dispatch.
Transactional state handling and role-based access control spanning nine operational roles.
projects.result: The system gives five departments one order record. Sales can see fulfillment per line item, warehouse works from goods receipts instead of manual logs, and dispatch waits for both warehouse and finance sign-off. The state machine keeps responsibility visible through the whole lifecycle.

projects.title: ECOBANK026 / WASTE BANK
projects.headline: A waste-bank ledger with guarded Excel imports and protected stock.
projects.problemHeadline: Deposits lived in spreadsheets. The ledger did not.
projects.problemLead: Dozens of date-separated spreadsheets made every deposit a manual reconciliation. Prices, stock, and audit history had no single source of truth.
projects.description: A Laravel operations system for a community waste bank. Deposits, withdrawals, and collector sales share one ledger, with dual pricing, guarded Excel imports, cumulative stock checks, and a multi-role audit trail.
projects.summary: Waste-bank records used to live in dozens of spreadsheets, with prices and stock reconciled by hand. The system puts deposits, withdrawals, and collector sales into one ledger, validates bulk imports, and blocks any sale that would make stock negative.
problemPoints: Deposit records were scattered across many date-based Excel sheets, and material labels were inconsistent (Paper, Used Paper, and Crumpled Paper all meant the same item), inviting duplicate categories and reports that contradicted each other.
Customer savings balances and the waste bank's cash were calculated by hand outside the transaction data, so there was no single source of truth when the two disagreed.
Aggregate sales to collectors could exceed the stock that actually existed, especially when entries were backdated, and there was no audit trail to trace the amounts or the people behind them.

overview.problem: Waste-bank records lived in date-separated Excel files, so every deposit was reconciled by hand. Item names were inconsistent (Paper, Used Paper, and Crumpled Paper meant the same material), customer savings and cash were tracked outside the transaction data, and collector sales could exceed stock. With no audit trail, a discrepancy was hard to trace.
overview.approach: The app is a Laravel service layer built around one ledger. BankSampahService handles financial logic and MaterialMappingService resolves material names. Deposits, withdrawals, and sales are state transitions that must pass validation before they reach the database. Customer savings and cash are derived from ledger entries instead of a mutable balance column. Prices are stored per transaction, so a master price change cannot rewrite history.
overview.architecture: Deposit, deposit detail, savings ledger, and cash ledger tables record every value movement. Writes run inside DB::transaction, and balances are recalculated from the ledger. Withdrawals require two prior deposits and cannot exceed the balance. Sales check cumulative stock across the whole timeline, including backdated entries, with lockForUpdate guarding concurrent writes. The activity log is append-only and tied to a correlation_id.
overview.workflow: An operator selects a customer and material, the form fills the master price, and the deposit is saved atomically with its ledger entry. Historical Excel files are parsed, mapped, previewed, and only committed when every row passes validation. A collector sale checks remaining stock, records the margin, and writes an audit entry.

flowPaths.title: Daily deposits
flowPaths.description: The primary path that runs every day when an operator records a waste deposit directly at the waste bank.

steps.name: Select Customer & Material
steps.action: The deposit form loads active customers and waste categories; the customer buy price (member_price) is filled automatically and can be overridden manually.

steps.name: Validate & Save Atomically
steps.action: DB::transaction writes the Deposit and each DepositDetail with its subtotal, rejecting any row without a waste_category_id or material_label.

steps.name: Record Credit Ledger
steps.action: Writes a savings_ledgers entry of type credit with reference_type/reference_id to the Deposit as the source of truth for the customer balance.

steps.name: Audit Trail After Commit
steps.action: A deposit.create activity log is written outside the transaction, carrying customer_name and total_amount so it is still recorded even if an exception occurs after commit.

flowPaths.title: Historical Excel import
flowPaths.description: The branch that loads thousands of legacy transaction rows from spreadsheets without dragging inconsistencies into the master data.

steps.name: Upload & Detect Structure
steps.action: listSheets and guessDateFromSheetName read each date-based sheet, then parseSheet detects the header row and the customer, material, weight, price, and total columns.

steps.name: Resolve Customers & Materials
steps.action: Material labels are resolved in layers: exact canonical, then scoped alias, then a new material; customers are matched by code or normalized name with ambiguity detection.

steps.name: Preview & Cross-Validate
steps.action: processRows computes price and total, and buildRecap verifies that material, customer, and transaction totals are consistent before commit; flagged rows are blocked.

steps.name: Commit in date order
steps.action: A single DB::transaction saves deposits per customer, syncs master prices, and stamps a fingerprint (md5 of file+sheet+date) so re-importing the same file is rejected.

flowPaths.title: Collector sale with stock check
flowPaths.description: The control applied before a collector sale is processed: it ensures stock never goes negative and the margin is recorded correctly.

steps.name: Read Remaining Stock
steps.action: getDailyRemainingWaste computes cumulative deposit weight minus sales per category up to the transaction date for the selected collector.

steps.name: Check stock across dates
steps.action: lockForUpdate on the stock row is followed by assertCumulativeStockNotNegative, which scans the whole timeline and rejects a sale that would make stock negative on any date.

steps.name: Compute Margin & Snapshot
steps.action: Subtotal and margin are rounded per detail; sale_details stores member_price and margin as a snapshot, and the waste bank's cash receives only the margin.

steps.name: Consistency Audit
steps.action: BankSampahAuditService scans for balance mismatches, duplicate ledger rows, negative balances, and orphan transactions, then produces a health score with an exit code.

workflowStages.name: MASTER & CUSTOMERS
workflowStages.detail: Prepares waste categories, material groups and aliases, plus customer buy prices and collector sell prices as transaction references.

workflowStages.name: DAILY TRANSACTIONS
workflowStages.detail: Records deposits, withdrawals (allowed only after two deposits), and collector sales with balance and stock validation.

workflowStages.name: LEDGER & CASH
workflowStages.detail: Every transaction writes a ledger entry; customer savings and the waste bank's cash balance are recomputed from the ledger.

workflowStages.name: AUDIT & REPORTS
workflowStages.detail: Append-only audit trail, a consistency health score, and exports for deposits, sales, the savings journal, and cash flow.

decisions.title: LEDGER AS SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH
decisions.decision: Do not store a directly mutable balance column; customer savings and cash are derived from the append-only savings_ledgers and waste_bank_cash_ledgers.
decisions.rationale: A mutable balance column opens a path to desynchronization when transactions are edited or deleted, and it makes reconciliation hard. With a ledger, every change is explained as a new entry and the balance can be recomputed at any time. The trade-off is that every write must consistently create both the primary transaction and the ledger entry within one DB::transaction.

decisions.title: DUAL PRICING WITH HISTORICAL SNAPSHOTS
decisions.decision: Store member_price and margin per sale_details row, separate from the WastePrice master, so the master price is never reused to reconstruct past data.
decisions.rationale: Storing only a reference to the master price lets a retroactive price change rewrite historical financial reports. A snapshot keeps history stable, while WastePriceHistory tracks price changes. The trade-off is duplicated values on detail rows and the need to keep them consistent during explicit overrides.

decisions.title: IDEMPOTENT EXCEL IMPORT WITH CROSS-VALIDATION
decisions.decision: Bulk import never inserts directly: rows are parsed, normalized, mapped, recomputed, cross-checked through a recap, and only then committed atomically with an anti-reimport fingerprint.
decisions.rationale: Raw spreadsheets are full of inconsistent labels, empty prices, and duplicate sheets. Without a validation stage, a single import could permanently pollute the master data and the financial history. The staged approach allows human review of ambiguous rows, at the cost of a longer, stateful import flow.

decisions.title: ATOMIC TRANSACTIONS WITH A FULL-TIMELINE STOCK GUARD
decisions.decision: A sale locks the stock row with lockForUpdate, aggregates weight per category, and validates remaining stock across the entire timeline through assertCumulativeStockNotNegative before writing.
decisions.rationale: Two concurrent sales, or a single backdated sale, can push cumulative stock negative without being detected. Scanning the timeline ensures no date point drops below zero, not just the ending balance. The cost is a heavier query and a longer lock on the sold category.

architectureLayers.name: CLIENT LAYER
items: ApexCharts for dashboard and report visualization

architectureLayers.name: BUSINESS & DOMAIN
items: State transitions and validation: dual pricing, margin, balance, and cumulative stock
Authorization: role-based permissions + admin device binding

architectureLayers.name: DATA & STORAGE
items: Eloquent ORM with ledger and transaction-detail relations

highlights: A full-timeline stock guard (assertCumulativeStockNotNegative) rejects any sale that would make stock negative on any date, including backdated transactions.
Atomic writes with DB::transaction and lockForUpdate prevent race conditions and double-selling between concurrent sales.
Role-based authorization is reinforced with admin device binding using revocable httpOnly tokens, so operational traces stay tied to a device.
An immutable, append-only audit trail with correlation_id and sanitized payloads; balances can be reconciled automatically through an anomaly-based health score.
projects.result: Every rupiah that enters or leaves the waste bank can be traced from the transaction to a ledger entry. Balance, stock, and import checks close the gaps that allowed over-selling and silent data drift. Price snapshots keep old reports stable when master prices change, and the audit trail keeps each action tied to a user and a device.

projects.title: SALESTRACK / PROPERTY LEAD DISPATCH
projects.headline: Time-boxed lead dispatch with client-server deadline enforcement.
projects.problemHeadline: Leads arrived with a deadline. The process had none.
projects.problemLead: Leads arrive from many channels and must be contacted within minutes. Handing them out over chat made ownership and response time impossible to measure.
projects.flowHeadline: One lead. A deadline enforced on both sides.
projects.description: A Flutter client for property sales teams. It pushes time-boxed leads to agents, enforces an accept-or-expire window, and tracks each lead from assignment to conversion with an auditable status history.
projects.summary: Property leads arrive from several channels and go cold in minutes. The app gives each agent a countdown to accept, enforces the same deadline on the server, and records every status change so managers can see what happened.
problemPoints: Leads were distributed manually over chat and spreadsheets, so ownership was ambiguous and two agents could contact the same prospect.
Acceptance deadlines lived in convention rather than code, so slow responses went undetected and could not be enforced or measured.
Without a server-committed accept step, client and backend could disagree on who owned a lead once it was reassigned after expiry.

overview.problem: Property sales teams get leads from social ads, WhatsApp, and property portals, and must contact them within minutes. Leads were handed out over chat and spreadsheets, so ownership was ambiguous and response time could not be measured. When several agents chase or drop the same lead, the prospect gets duplicate calls and conversion data stops making sense. The deadline also has to hold when the agent's phone is asleep or the app is backgrounded, which a UI-only timer cannot do.
overview.approach: Each incoming lead is a time-boxed state machine. IncomingLeadProvider records the arrival time and resolved timeout, then derives remaining time from the wall clock instead of decrementing a counter. Timeout resolution checks the push payload, then the agent profile, then a hard default. Acceptance is a server commit via POST /leads/{id}/accept; the client only removes the pending lead after the server confirms ownership.
overview.architecture: The app is split into feature modules (auth, dashboard, leads, incoming_lead, notifications, profile) over shared API, model, and service layers. Every request goes through one ApiService that attaches the bearer token, injects the mobile user id, enforces a 30-second timeout, and normalizes errors. A 401 on any non-auth endpoint clears all providers and resets navigation. Notifications use two Android channels: a normal channel, and a max-importance channel reserved for incoming leads with full-screen intent and a custom sound.
overview.workflow: The backend assigns a lead and pushes a data message to the agent. The device classifies the message, raises a full-screen alert with the countdown, and registers the lead. If the agent accepts before the deadline, the server commits ownership and the lead moves to the active list. Otherwise the timer expires and the lead is released for re-dispatch. Once owned, the agent moves the lead through contacted, interested or not_interested, and converted or rejected, with notes shown in the activity timeline.

flowPaths.title: Lead accepted
flowPaths.description: Runs when a high-priority lead is dispatched and the agent accepts within the auto-reject window.

steps.name: Push Dispatch
steps.action: Backend emits a data message tagged type=lead_assigned with priority=high; the client classifies it as an incoming lead.

steps.name: Full-Screen Alert
steps.action: Raises a max-importance notification with fullScreenIntent, starts looping lead_alert audio, and opens IncomingLeadScreen with leadId and timeout.

steps.name: Countdown syncs with server
steps.action: Provider registers arrivalTime, derives remaining seconds from the wall clock, and the screen enriches fields from GET /mobile/leads/{id}.

steps.name: Accept Persist
steps.action: POST /mobile/leads/{id}/accept commits ownership; the provider removes the pending lead, stops the sound, and routes to /leads.

flowPaths.title: Deadline expires
flowPaths.description: Runs when the agent does not act before the deadline and the lead must be released.

steps.name: Window Exhausted
steps.action: The 1-second scheduler marks the lead expired when now exceeds arrivalTime + timeoutSeconds and prunes it from the pending list.

steps.name: UI Teardown
steps.action: The screen detects remainingSeconds at zero, cancels its timer, stops the audio player, and pops itself.

steps.name: Runtime Notice
steps.action: A snackbar reports the lead was auto-declined and the incoming badge disappears from the dashboard.

steps.name: Backend Re-Dispatch
steps.action: The assignment record transitions to expired and the backend reassigns the lead to the next eligible agent.

flowPaths.title: Session expires
flowPaths.description: Every request passes through a single authentication boundary that invalidates the whole session on expiry.

steps.name: Request Signing
steps.action: Attaches the Bearer token and auto-injects userId for /mobile/* endpoints from persisted session state.

steps.name: Token Validation
steps.action: Validates the token and returns HTTP 401 for expired or invalid credentials.

steps.name: Session cleared
steps.action: A 401 on any non-auth endpoint clears the Auth, Leads, Dashboard, Notification, and IncomingLead providers before proceeding.

steps.name: Session Purge
steps.action: Persisted credentials are cleared and the navigator resets to /login, preventing stale-state access.

workflowStages.name: LEAD INGESTION
workflowStages.detail: A lead is captured from a channel and queued for assignment to an eligible agent.

workflowStages.name: PUSH ASSIGNMENT
workflowStages.detail: A high-priority data message is pushed to the assigned agent's device.

workflowStages.name: ACCEPT GATE
workflowStages.detail: The agent must accept within the profile-defined window; the deadline is enforced client and server side.

workflowStages.name: STATUS LIFECYCLE
workflowStages.detail: Lead advances through contacted, interested or not_interested, then converted or rejected with notes.

decisions.title: WALL-CLOCK COUNTDOWN INSTEAD OF A DECREMENTING TIMER
decisions.decision: IncomingLeadProvider stores arrivalTime and derives remainingSeconds from DateTime.now() on read, while a single 1-second timer only schedules re-render and pruning.
decisions.rationale: A decrementing counter drifts or freezes when the OS suspends the app or backgrounds the process. Deriving from the wall clock keeps the deadline consistent across foreground, background, and screen re-entry, and makes the timer a scheduler rather than a source of truth.

decisions.title: DUAL FCM CHANNELS WITH A CENTRALIZED CLASSIFIER
decisions.decision: Two Android channels are declared at startup: a normal channel and a max-importance fullScreenIntent channel, and a single isIncomingLead() classifier decides routing for foreground, background, and terminated states.
decisions.rationale: Android channel importance is immutable after creation, so urgent lead alerts require a dedicated channel that cannot be reused for routine notifications. Centralizing classification prevents three divergent interpretations of the same payload and reserves fullScreenIntent and custom sound strictly for high-priority leads.

decisions.title: TYPED MODEL LAYER WITH NULL-SAFE NESTED ADAPTERS
decisions.decision: Every API response is parsed into typed Dart models (LeadModel, DashboardModel, UserProfile) with defensive fromJson casting, and the UI never indexes raw maps.
decisions.rationale: The backend returns inconsistent shapes: wrapped data, nested source/property/assignments objects, nullable timestamps. Parsing at the boundary turns runtime cast failures into controlled defaults (empty lists, fallbacks) and decouples UI rebuilds from transport-format changes.

decisions.title: GLOBAL SESSION INTERCEPTOR IN THE HTTP LAYER
decisions.decision: ApiService centrally injects the Bearer token and userId and converts any 401 on a non-auth endpoint into a full logout that clears all ChangeNotifier providers.
decisions.rationale: Scattering auth handling across features leaves orphaned state and half-authenticated screens. A single interceptor guarantees that an expired token purges cached leads, dashboard, notifications, and pending alerts atomically, preventing stale data from leaking after session expiry.

architectureLayers.name: CLIENT LAYER
items: Provider / ChangeNotifier with Selector and AutomaticKeepAliveClientMixin
Typed fromJson model adapters (no runtime map casting)

architectureLayers.name: BUSINESS & DOMAIN
items: Layered feature modules (auth, dashboard, leads, incoming_lead, notifications, profile)
IncomingLeadProvider deadline engine with status lifecycle (assigned → contacted → interested → converted/rejected)
Role/session model with global 401 invalidation and userId auto-injection
Debug-gated request/response logging with diagnostic hints

architectureLayers.name: DATA & STORAGE
items: Central ApiService with per-domain clients (leads, dashboard, profile, devices, notifications)
Firebase Cloud Messaging with two notification channels
Session persistence with atomic clear on logout or 401

highlights: Deadline-based incoming lead engine that derives remaining time from the wall clock, so countdowns survive app suspension and screen re-entry without drift.
Payload classifier with dedicated high-priority channel delivering fullScreenIntent, custom lead_alert sound, and looping audio only for urgent assignments.
Centralized 401 interceptor that atomically purges Auth, Leads, Dashboard, Notification, and IncomingLead providers before resetting navigation to login.
Typed boundary parsing of nested, nullable API payloads (source, property, assignments) with time-bound caches and optimistic lead updates.
projects.result: Deadlines and ownership are enforced the same way on the device and on the server, instead of being inferred from chat threads. Agents see one prioritized incoming alert with a countdown, and every accepted lead carries an auditable sequence of assignment and status changes. Managers get dashboard metrics from that consistent state, and the app stays predictable through backgrounding, poor connectivity, and token expiry.

projects.title: ECARRGO
projects.headline: A logistics reverse-auction marketplace with a controlled shipment state machine.
projects.problemHeadline: Rates were negotiated in chat. The shipment had no single owner.
projects.problemLead: Shipping ran through intermediaries with no structured record. Prices were hard to compare, and one order could be held by more than one vendor.
projects.flowHeadline: One shipment. A controlled auction state machine.
projects.description: A two-role mobile app that turns shipping orders into a rate auction. Senders post an order, logistics vendors bid, and the system locks the winner, payment, and tracking into one status flow.
projects.summary: Senders post a shipment, vendors bid, and the lowest offer wins. The app locks the winner, payment, and tracking into one status flow so an order cannot be claimed twice or lose its owner.
problemPoints: Shipping rates were negotiated manually over chat and phone, so prices went unrecorded, could not be compared, and orders were at risk of being placed with more than one vendor.
With no single source, shipment_id, auction_id, and waybill number were easily swapped between the fill-in, payment, and tracking screens, breaking the integrity chain of the shipment data.
Transfer proofs were received without a record tying them to a transaction, so payment verification depended on manual matching by an admin and could not be audited.

overview.problem: Shipping used to run through intermediaries: senders contacted several vendors and negotiated prices with no structured record. At volume that breaks down. Prices cannot be compared, one order can be held by more than one vendor, and shipment status has no single authority. When the vendor, sender, and admin see different states, an order stalls with no clear owner.
overview.approach: The system is a reverse-auction marketplace with the shipment as the aggregate root. A sender posts an order with a price limit and duration, vendors bid, and the sender picks a winner. The system then locks the price, creates an invoice, and drives status through fixed transitions. The UI recomputes its step from the server status, so navigation follows backend authority instead of a client cache.
overview.architecture: The Flutter client separates data sources, domain, and presentation, with Dio handling transport and bearer tokens. A single FillDataProvider collects the whole wizard before sending one auction payload, so partial orders cannot leave the device. On the server, shipment status is the source of truth, and the select-winner, payment, and tracking endpoints enforce per-owner authorization. Status history is kept as an audit trail.
overview.workflow: The sender picks a route on the map, enters cargo details, sets the auction against a rate reference, and submits the order. Vendors bid, the sender selects a winner, and an admin confirms the price and starts shipping. After the sender uploads a transfer proof and an admin verifies it, the status moves to shipping, and waybill tracking closes the loop until completion.

flowPaths.title: Order Creation & Auction
flowPaths.description: Runs when a sender creates a new shipment and the system must produce one shipment with one linked auction.

steps.name: Select Route & Schedule
steps.action: The app captures pickup and destination points via map and geolocation, then stores the schedule in FillDataProvider.

steps.name: Enter Cargo Details
steps.action: Per-item validation rejects weight over 100 tons, or empty volume or value, before the data is provisionally locked.

steps.name: Set Auction Parameters
steps.action: Fetches a rate reference from the generate-rates endpoint and ensures the auction duration does not exceed the shipping time.

steps.name: Submit Order
steps.action: POST /auctions creates the shipment and auction together, returning auction_id, shipment_id, and resi_number that are shared to the providers.

flowPaths.title: Vendor Bidding & Winner Selection
flowPaths.description: Runs while the auction is active until exactly one vendor is selected as the order winner.

steps.name: Browse Auctions
steps.action: The vendor pulls the list of active auctions and filters by route and estimated order value.

steps.name: Submit a Bid
steps.action: The bid is recorded with bid_amount and status, allowing sorting by lowest, highest, or newest.

steps.name: Select Winner
steps.action: PATCH /auctions/{id}/select-winner sets vendor_id and locks the winner so the order is not held by two parties.

steps.name: Confirm Price
steps.action: The admin confirms the price and moves the auction status toward auction_started as the payment start point.

flowPaths.title: Payment & Verified Tracking
flowPaths.description: The authorization, payment verification, and audit trail that must be passed before a shipment is marked complete.

steps.name: Authentication & Token
steps.action: Login returns access_token and role; the token is stored in secure storage and injected as a Bearer header on every request.

steps.name: Upload Transfer Proof
steps.action: The image is sent as multipart with Authorization and a site-password; the file name is used as a traceable transaction_id.

steps.name: Create Payment Record
steps.action: POST /payments stores amount, method, and a pending status that binds shipment_id and the paying user_id.

steps.name: Verify & Track
steps.action: After verification, the status becomes shipping and waybill tracking shows status_history as an audit trail until completed.

workflowStages.name: CONFIRMATION
workflowStages.detail: Status waiting_approval: CS verifies identity, shipment data, and order eligibility.

workflowStages.name: AUCTION & PAYMENT
workflowStages.detail: Status auction_started: bidding runs, a winner is chosen, then the payment proof is uploaded.

workflowStages.name: EN ROUTE
workflowStages.detail: Status shipping: the package is in transit and the status is recorded on the waybill tracking.

workflowStages.name: DELIVERED
workflowStages.detail: Status completed: shipping is finished and the order is confirmed as received.

decisions.title: SERVER STATUS AS A STATE MACHINE, NOT A CLIENT CACHE
decisions.decision: UI steps are recomputed from the shipment status on the server, and local progress cache is reset when it is not backed by a confirmation.
decisions.rationale: If the client decides its own steps, an order can stall on a stale step after the server status changed. Mapping status to steps and validating the cache keeps navigation consistent with backend authority even when the app is closed mid-flow.

decisions.title: ONE ACCUMULATOR PROVIDER FOR THE MULTI-STEP WIZARD
decisions.decision: All five steps of input are stored in a single FillDataProvider with per-step validation before the payload is sent.
decisions.rationale: Sending data per step invites partial orders and orphan shipment_ids. A single accumulation ensures the auction is created only when every field is valid, at the cost of holding wizard state longer on the client.

decisions.title: REVERSE AUCTION WITH SERVER-SIDE WINNER LOCKING
decisions.decision: Winner selection happens through the sender's select-winner endpoint, not free negotiation on the client.
decisions.rationale: A reverse auction lowers prices naturally, but without locking, one order can be held by many vendors. A dedicated endpoint ensures only the order owner sets the winner and prevents double assignment.

decisions.title: SECURE TOKENS AND AUTH-BOUND DEVICE SYNC
decisions.decision: The access token is stored in secure storage with centralized Bearer injection, and the FCM token is registered following the login cycle.
decisions.rationale: Storing the token in plain storage or spreading headers across every call increases leak risk and inconsistency. Centralized injection simplifies authorization, while post-login device-token registration keeps notifications reaching the right user.

architectureLayers.name: CLIENT LAYER
items: Secure token and local session storage

architectureLayers.name: BUSINESS & DOMAIN
items: Data source layer + Dio HTTP client

architectureLayers.name: DATA & STORAGE
items: Secure storage for the access token
Object storage for transfer proofs + status_history as audit trail

highlights: UI steps are recomputed from server status and the local progress cache is reset when unconfirmed, avoiding users stuck on a stale step after a status change.
Layered per-step validation (maximum weight 100 tons and auction duration not exceeding the shipping time) rejects inconsistent auction payloads before they are sent.
Winner selection through an owner-only endpoint with a transaction_id derived from the payment proof file name, traceable back to the record.
Status transitions are recorded as status_history on the waybill tracking and rendered back into a user-side timeline.
projects.result: ECARRGO turns manually negotiated shipping into a structured auction flow with one status authority on the server. Every order has a linked shipment and auction, one selected winner, and a payment that can be verified through a traceable transfer proof. Mapping status to flow steps keeps the process resumable across sessions, and the status audit trail gives operations a clear record as volume grows.
